question.text: Kaveri Capital Partners II, a SEBI-registered Category II AIF, is finalising its PPM. The Investment Manager is drafting the Management Fee clause. Per market practice for Indian Cat I/II AIFs, during the COMMITMENT PERIOD, the management fee is typically levied as a percentage of which base?

answer.text: Gross NAV (GNAV) of the fund computed each quarter
Committed Capital (whether drawn down or not)
Net Asset Value post management-fee deduction
Realised IRR of exited portfolio investments only

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 is explicit: for Cat I and II AIFs, Management Fees during the Commitment Period are charged as a percentage of COMMITTED CAPITAL. After the commitment period, the base typically transitions to Invested Capital (actual cost basis) or GNAV. Committed-capital fees incentivise the GP to deploy the capital they promised. The Trap: Option A (GNAV) is the POST-commitment-period base for some funds and is tempting; Option C describes a circular definition; Option D is hedge-fund / Cat III style realised-return fee logic — irrelevant to the management-fee base. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests the same clause from a distributor's angle (explaining LP economics). XIX-C covered this across all categories; XIX-E (Cat III) would frame the base as daily NAV on a series-of-units basis — not testable at Cat I/II level. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating LPAs, sophisticated LPs push for 'management fees on invested capital net of write-downs' post the commitment period — this reduces GP fee drag on under-deployed vintages. Always model both committed-capital and invested-capital scenarios when quoting the total fee load to LPs.
